system_description.narrative_title: Russia's military-diplomatic push and global geopolitical strain
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is Russia's use of military force, diplomatic vetoes, and global outreach to reshape outcomes in Ukraine and beyond, provoking arms transfers, institutional deadlock, and new partner alignments. As an open system, it comprises cross-border flows of force, intelligence, arms, information, energy deals, and diplomatic signals that enter from external actors (U.S., EU, G20, African states, corporations) and produce outputs such as ceasefires, sanctions, vetoed resolutions, and regional realignments. Key feedbacks are visible: strikes and occupation drive allied arms sales and political pressure, which in turn shape Ukrainian tactics and international negotiations; simultaneously, Russian outreach (e.g., nuclear deals, diplomatic maneuvers) seeks to offset isolation. The situation dynamically interacts with related arenas (European security, energy markets, international institutions) and adapts through pauses, resumptions, and bargaining.
system_description.scope: Inside: the Russia–Ukraine conflict and its immediate international linkages — Russian military strikes and occupation, Ukrainian military and political responses (including ceasefires/evacuations), arms transfers and defense industry activity, diplomatic interactions at the G20/UN/Turkey, energy and corporate ties (oil, gas, nuclear deals), intelligence and information operations, and humanitarian impacts in affected locales (e.g., Oleshky). Included actors: Russia, Ukraine, U.S., EU states, NATO, G20, UN, Turkey, African partner states, private firms (defense, energy, tech), and local populations.
system_description.super_system: The global international order / geopolitical and security architecture (great-power competition, global governance, and energy-security systems).
adjacent_subsystems: European security architecture (NATO, EU defense and political coordination)
Global energy and commodity markets (oil, gas, nuclear investment)
International institutions and diplomacy (UN Security Council, G20, ceasefire negotiation fora)
Private-sector defense and tech ecosystems (arms manufacturers, satellite/communications providers, energy firms)

variables.name: Military force projection
variables.description: The intensity and capacity of cross-border conventional military operations and occupation affecting contested areas.

variables.name: Diplomatic leverage
variables.description: The ability of actors to shape international negotiations, forum outcomes, and bilateral bargaining through diplomatic means.

variables.name: Arms transfer rate
variables.description: The tempo and volume of weapon and materiel deliveries moving into conflict zones or between external supporters.

variables.name: Institutional deadlock level
variables.description: The degree to which multilateral decision-making bodies are paralyzed by vetoes, procedural blocks, or lack of consensus.

variables.name: Energy deal engagement
variables.description: The rate and depth of cross-border energy agreements, investments, and contractual ties linking parties in the system.

variables.name: Information influence
variables.description: The prevalence and reach of information operations, media pressure, and narrative shaping that alter public and elite perceptions.

variables.name: Territorial control
variables.description: The proportion and stability of geographic areas under de facto control by contesting forces.

variables.name: Humanitarian displacement rate
variables.description: The flow rate of civilians evacuated, displaced, or otherwise moving as a result of hostilities and related disruptions.

variables.name: Ceasefire stability
variables.description: The durability and probability that local truces and pauses in fighting will hold over time.

variables.name: Defense industry capacity
variables.description: The production and logistical capacity of arms producers to supply platforms, munitions, and support systems.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: The degree of policy alignment, burden-sharing, and coordinated action among groups of aligned actors.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure
variables.description: The intensity, scope, and enforcement of economic and financial restrictions applied to target parties.

variables.name: Intelligence activity level
variables.description: The tempo and intensity of intelligence collection, covert operations, and information exchange related to the conflict.

variables.name: Nuclear engagement risk
variables.description: The likelihood and scale of nuclear-related cooperation, transactions, or escalatory signaling that alter strategic stability.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: The variability of global energy prices and supply-disruption risk driven by conflict-related flows and policy actions.

variables.name: Corporate financial exposure
variables.description: The extent of commercial investments, contractual ties, and balance-sheet exposure of private actors to counterparties in the system.

catalysts.title: Zelenskiy visits Turkey for talks
catalysts.description: Ukrainian president's planned trip to Turkey for negotiations and mediation could shift diplomatic momentum and influence ceasefire or security discussions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Zelenskiy says he will head to Turkey for talks'; mediation potential cited in coverage.

catalysts.title: US Patriot missile sale deliveries to Ukraine
catalysts.description: Following US approval of a $2.1bn Patriot sale, deliveries and integration into Ukrainian defenses will raise air-defense capacity over coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine' implies forthcoming deliveries and integration.

catalysts.title: Russia-Rosatom nuclear talks in Africa
catalysts.description: Rosatom negotiations with multiple African states on large nuclear plants may deepen energy ties and Russian diplomatic footholds on the continent.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Russia in talks with four African states on large nuclear power plants, Rosatom says' and 'Ghana says Russia to back 2,000 MW nuclear plant'.

catalysts.title: Continued UN Security Council deadlock
catalysts.description: Competing Russia-US resolutions and repeated vetoes signal ongoing paralysis in UNSC decision-making on related crises.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia vetos US-drafted resolution on Western Sahara' and 'Competing US, Russia resolutions... defeated'.

catalysts.title: Local ceasefires and evacuations in frontline areas
catalysts.description: Recent local pauses and evacuations (e.g., Oleshky) may expand or collapse, affecting civilian displacement and short-term front-line dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia and Ukraine begin local ceasefire in frontline city', 'Evacuees from Russian-occupied city arrive in Ukraine', 'Aid convoy sets off for Oleshky'.

catalysts.title: G20 foreign ministers meeting with Russia tensions
catalysts.description: G20 meetings marked by objections to Russia and skipped photo-ops could accentuate diplomatic rifts and hamper coordinated responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'G20 foreign ministers skip photo-op amid objections over Russia' and 'Rifts over wars in Ukraine, Middle East loom over G20 meeting in US'.

catalysts.title: Ongoing US pressure shaping Ukrainian targeting
catalysts.description: US diplomatic pressure to pause attacks on Russian refineries (and subsequent defiance) implies continued external influence on Ukrainian strike decisions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Russian Refineries After Pressure From U.S.' and 'Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Ending Pause and Defying Trump'.

catalysts.title: Slovak probe into fighter jet donation reopens
catalysts.description: A reopened Slovak prosecutor investigation into fighter jet donations could delay or complicate transfer decisions and political support.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Slovak prosecutor reopens probe into fighter jet donation to Ukraine' suggests legal delays to transfers.

catalysts.title: Executive departures and corporate pullback from gas venture
catalysts.description: Executives quitting a $25bn gas venture amid claims of hidden Russian control signals a broader risk of corporate divestment and deal unwinding.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US executives quit $25bn gas venture over claims of secret Russian control' indicates deal reputational and financial fallout.

catalysts.title: Closure of independent media and tighter information control
catalysts.description: Shuttering of Russia's last major independent newspaper signals deeper state control over media and information operations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Russia’s last major independent newspaper shuts under government pressure' implies increased state narrative control.

catalysts.title: Ukrainian arms maker claims independence from SpaceX
catalysts.description: Fire Point's claim that systems can operate without SpaceX could reduce external dependence and accelerate indigenous strike and ISR capabilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Ukrainian arms maker Fire Point says its systems can complete missions without SpaceX' signals growing domestic capability.
